title: Exact group invariant scar towers in two dimensional gauge theories
authors: João Barata, Kiryl Pakrouski, Andrey V. Sadofyev
abstract: We construct exact many-body scar towers in two dimensional gauge theories with two flavors of massless fundamental fermions. For oppositely charged fermions, the scar subspace is generated by a gauge-neutral $η$-pairing operator, and admits a purely algebraic construction. Exact diagonalization methods reveal anomalously low entanglement and long-range pair correlations in the scar states. Charge conjugation maps the $η$-tower to a vector-flavor polarization sector of the equal charge model, yielding an interpretation as a coherent flavor mode with Josephson-like phase dynamics. Finite fermion masses mix the protected pair with an orthogonal channel and destroy the exact tower. The identified scar tower can be algebraically realized in a large family of lattice field theories, revealing a universal character of these states. Our results provide an analytical construction of invariant scar subspaces in a gauge theory with a nontrivial continuum interpretation.
summary: This work provides an analytical construction of exact, gauge-invariant many-body scar states in 2D gauge theories. These states are characterized by suppressed entanglement and exhibit coherent, Josephson-like dynamics governed by a conserved pseudo-spin symmetry. The findings suggest a universal mechanism for non-thermal behavior in quantum field theories.
main_problem: The paper addresses the open question of how out-of-equilibrium states in quantum gauge field theories lose memory of initial conditions, focusing on the persistence of exceptional, athermal states known as quantum many-body scars.
main_result: The authors construct an exact, algebraically defined tower of gauge-invariant scar states in 2D gauge theories, showing they exhibit anomalously low entanglement and long-range correlations.
method: The construction relies on identifying a symmetry-generating algebra (using an $\eta$-pairing operator) that annihilates the scar subspace, which is then analyzed using exact diagonalization and bosonization techniques.
model_or_system: The primary model is two-dimensional gauge theories, specifically the massless two-flavor Schwinger model ($QED(q, -q)_2$), analyzed on a lattice.
key_observables: Anomalously low bipartite entanglement entropy, long-range pair correlations, and coherent flavor precession dynamics ($\dot{\vartheta} = \Delta$).
important_parameters: Fermion masses ($m_f$), the chemical potential bias ($\Delta$), and the lattice spacing ($a$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a conserved pseudo-spin symmetry that protects the scar subspace, and it notes that finite fermion masses break this exact protection.
figures_summary: Figures numerically compare entanglement entropy and two-point correlation functions for scar states versus thermal averages, and map the $\eta'$ scar tower under various transformations.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general problem of ETH violation to the specific construction of the scar tower using algebraic methods, analyzing its properties (low entanglement, correlations) and its dynamics (Josephson-like precession) under symmetry-preserving and symmetry-breaking perturbations.
why_interesting: The concept of protected, non-thermal states (scars) is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems, offering an analytical handle on deviations from thermalization.
